title: i have a lot to say on wicked #wickedmovie #wickedforgood #wickedthem...
transcript: Does wicked for good fix the problems of Wicked Act 2? It is officially wicked for good release day. If you haven't watched the film yet, maybe bookmark this video and come back to it after you've seen it. If wicked is Elphaba story to becoming wicked, then wicked for good is Glinda story to becoming good. Which, of course, I would argue that Elphaba is never truly wicked, in the same way that I would argue that Glinda is never truly good, although I think she wants to be. And wicked for good is able to explicitly lean into this idea in the way that wicked Act 2 never really has been able to. Because let's be real, wicked Act 2 has always been the problem child of wicked. Timeline is unclear. The motivations we're not 100% sure of, but there are so many bangers in Act 2, including all three of my favorite songs from wicked, that I've always been a bit of an act II apologist. And I think they showed us that the expanded run time helps so much. We get so much more into the psychology of Glinda and Elphaba, which I love. Elphaba and her rage for the animals, her justifiable anger. Glinda and her fear and her cowardness of not wanting to rock the boat. I love that you get more of the two of them together, where you really see their bond and their love and their caring for each other. Ariana Grande is Unbelievable. She's giving an incredibly beautiful, nuanced acting performance. Obviously, Cynthia Erivo is unbelievable. One of the greatest musical theatre actors alive. Her no good deed is definitive. And I gotta mention Jonathan Bailey because the acting performance that he is giving with just his eyes alone, I cannot stop thinking about. Thank goodness. And watching him as Ariana sounds like a literal goddess. She looks amazing. And he is just doing things with his eyes where you know exactly what he is thinking, exactly what he is feeling, without him having to say a word. I like that. We also get to see more of the politics of Oz, how the Yellow Brick road was basically built in the back of slave labor . The scene where Boq is trying to leave Munchkinland and he is literally turned away at the train station is devastating. And Ethan is giving an incredible performance. Also, my biggest plot things is how Elphaba flies to MunchkinLand, and then the same time, Fiyero also gets to MunchkinLand, but we never see how And this one, they explained it. Same with how Glinda gets to Elphaba before for good. One of my biggest problems with wicked is at the end of the show when Glinda tells Elphaba “I will tell them everything. I will let them know the truth.” And Elphaba says, “no, they'll turn against you”. And Glinda goes, “I don't care.” And Elphaba goes, “promise me.” And Glinda goes, “okay, I Don't understand. But sure.” And I've always been like, ask why? And in the movie, they do. And then, of course, the door scene, which has wrecked me in ways I can never explain. There are many moments that I prefer in the stage show, and I think that is okay. It is a different medium. Ultimately, I really, really like the movie as a part two to the original film. It's not a sequel. It is a part two. And I think that that is the big thing that people need to wrap their minds around. So, no, I don't think wicked for good has fixed Wicked Act II but I do think it has improved it significantly. Really just recommend watching it right after wicked for good, because when I saw it Monday versus when I saw it yesterday as a double feature, I very much changed my opinion on it. But I feel like this will be the first of many, many, many videos on wicked for good. But I'm very, very happy overall with the film, and I will be seeing it many times.
classificationReason: Explicitly about the Wicked for Good film ('release day,' 'expanded run time,' 'film'). Compares it to Act 2 of the stage show but the primary content is a film review, not a stage production review.
